aria: Animated recap of the Knicks' 121 to 102 home win over Cleveland: Jose Alvarado's go-ahead 3-pointer with 10:31 left that made it 87 to 85, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Alvarado's 21 points off the bench, the top scorers, how the Knicks won, and the next game.

figure.label: Jose Alvarado, listed 6-0, 179 lb (Wikipedia, Basketball-Reference); no sourced wingspan

notes: Box score from the CBS Sports gametracker and DigestSports for the Knicks' 121–102 home win over Cleveland on Nov 25, 2026: all 121 New York points and all 102 Cleveland points add up from the player lines, as do the shooting totals (46 of 90, 17 of 37 from three, 12 of 15 FT for New York; 35 of 85, 10 of 38, 22 of 28 for Cleveland). The quarter scores (23–33–26–39 to 34–27–24–17) are the same on CBS, DigestSports and HoopsNightly; 61–56 Cleveland at the half follows from them, and 85–82 Cleveland after three is in the AP and on CBS. New York's biggest lead (19) and Cleveland's (11) are on HoopsNightly; the AP also has Cleveland up 11 in the first half and again in the third. Bench points (45–21) are on HoopsNightly and add up from the box with the starters VAVEL lists (Towns, Hart, Bridges, Shamet, Brunson; Allen, Harden, Mitchell, Merrill, Watson). Josh Hart's assists differ between sources (12 in the AP and DigestSports, 11 on CBS), so they are left out. Records are from the game stories (Knicks 12–6, Cavaliers 9–10, AP); ranks are from the site's standings after Wednesday's games.

The Knicks have won six straight (AP; NY Post; Field Level Media). They outscored Cleveland 25–9 to start the fourth quarter for a 107–94 lead (AP), opening with a 12–0 run during which Cleveland went 0 for 8 with three turnovers (Field Level Media; Posting and Toasting). Alvarado scored 16 of his 21 in the fourth (Cleveland.com; NY Post; Posting and Toasting). OG Anunoby, Miles McBride and Jordan Clarkson did not play for New York (AP); Evan Mobley missed his seventh straight game for Cleveland (Cleveland.com). Next: the Knicks host Miami on Friday in their last NBA Cup group game (AP; Posting and Toasting); Cleveland hosts Miami on Sunday (AP; Cleveland.com).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Jose Alvarado's 3-pointer with 10:31 left that put the Knicks ahead 87–85: the CBS Sports play-by-play has "Jose Alvarado makes three point jump shot (Josh Hart assists)" at 10:31 of the fourth, right after Hart's driving layup at 11:08 made it 85–84, and "Jose Alvarado makes three point running jump shot (Josh Hart assists)" at 10:12 for 90–85. Field Level Media: Alvarado drained 3-pointers on consecutive possessions in the run that gave New York the lead for good; AP: Alvarado made consecutive 3-pointers for a 90–85 lead. So the board's Cavaliers +1 to Knicks +2 is 85–84 to 87–85. The shot's spot isn't described, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up from the arc. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the New York Knicks or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Alvarado's listed 6-foot-0 and 179 pounds (Wikipedia; Basketball-Reference), with arms at the default length because neither reports a wingspan, in the Knicks' home kit with No. 5 (Wikipedia) and the default darker skin tone, since he has no approved look yet. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
